greek: Σαρα δὲ ἡ γυνὴ Αβραμ οὐκ ἔτικτεν αὐτῷ. ἦν δὲ αὐτῇ παιδίσκη Αἰγυπτία, ᾗ ὄνομα Αγαρ.
hint: Sarai bears Abram no children; she has an Egyptian maid, Hagar.

notes.text: The word Paul uses of Hagar at Galatians 4:22, ἕνα ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης καὶ ἕνα ἐκ τῆς ἐλευθέρας, and whose name he reads at 4:24–25, ἥτις ἐστὶν Ἁγάρ.
ἦν with a dative of possession, plain `was`, as at 13:5.
The people's name in the feminine; glossed, like Αἰγύπτιοι at 12:14, as a name.

reading: [[name:Σαρα]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of [[name:Αβραμ]] not [[was bringing into the world|was bringing into the world, was bringing forth, was bearing, was producing|τίκτω]] to him. was [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], to her [[a young girl|a young girl, a maiden, a young slave, a courtesan|παιδίσκη]] [[name:Αἰγυπτία]], to whom [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[name:Αγαρ]].

names.gloss: (Σαρα, from Hebrew Śāray, usually connected with śārâ, "princess")
(Αβραμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrām, "the father is exalted")
(Αγαρ, from Hebrew Hāgār, of uncertain meaning)

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Σαρα πρὸς Αβραμ Ἰδοὺ συνέκλεισέν με κύριος τοῦ μὴ τίκτειν· εἴσελθε οὖν πρὸς τὴν παιδίσκην μου, ἵνα τεκνοποιήσῃς ἐξ αὐτῆς. ὑπήκουσεν δὲ Αβραμ τῆς φωνῆς Σαρας.
hint: Sarai gives Abram her maid, that he may have children by her.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾûlay ʾibbāneh mimmennâ*, *perhaps I shall be built up from her*, of Sarai. The Greek has *that you may bear children from her*, of Abram.
τεκνοποιέω, one sense, plain text, as at 11:30.
The article before the infinitive is not printed, as at 5:4.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads αὐτῆς for Σαρας.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ λαβοῦσα Σαρα ἡ γυνὴ Αβραμ Αγαρ τὴν Αἰγυπτίαν τὴν ἑαυτῆς παιδίσκην — μετὰ δέκα ἔτη τοῦ οἰκῆσαι Αβραμ ἐν γῇ Χανααν — καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν Αβραμ τῷ ἀνδρὶ αὐτῆς αὐτῷ γυναῖκα.
hint: After ten years in Canaan, Sarai gives Hagar to Abram as wife.

notes.text: Rahlfs sets the clause between dashes; the reading keeps it in commas, since dashes mark the chains.
The participle is followed by καί and the finite verb, as the Hebrew *wattiqqaḥ … wattittēn* has two verbs.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads τῷ ἀνδρί … Αβραμ, the other way round; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has Αβραμ first.

names.gloss: (Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς Αγαρ, καὶ συνέλαβεν. καὶ εἶδεν ὅτι ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχει, καὶ ἠτιμάσθη ἡ κυρία ἐναντίον αὐτῆς.
hint: Hagar conceives, and her mistress is slighted in her eyes.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wattēqal gĕbirtāh bĕʿênêhā*, *her mistress was light in her eyes*. The Greek has *was dishonoured before her*.
γαστήρ is first *the paunch, belly*; Middle Liddell gives ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχειν, *to be with child*, under its last sense, *the womb*.
Filed under κύριος, whose noun sense has ἡ κυρία, *mistress* or *lady of the house*.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Σαρα πρὸς Αβραμ Ἀδικοῦμαι ἐκ σοῦ· ἐγὼ δέδωκα τὴν παιδίσκην μου εἰς τὸν κόλπον σου, ἰδοῦσα δὲ ὅτι ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχει, ἠτιμάσθην ἐναντίον αὐτῆς· κρίναι ὁ θεὸς ἀνὰ μέσον ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ.
hint: Sarai: I am wronged by you; may God judge between us.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ḥămāsî ʿālêkā*, *my wrong be on you*. The Greek has *I am wronged by you*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *yišpōṭ YHWH*. The Greek has ὁ θεός.
ἀδικέω's first sense, *to do wrong*, takes no object that a passive could make its subject; *to do one wrong, to wrong*, heads the passive, and the first follows in its own voice.
The aorist optative, `may pick out`: κρίνω is first *to pick out, choose*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Αβραμ πρὸς Σαραν Ἰδοὺ ἡ παιδίσκη σου ἐν ταῖς χερσίν σου· χρῶ αὐτῇ, ὡς ἄν σοι ἀρεστὸν ᾖ. καὶ ἐκάκωσεν αὐτὴν Σαρα, καὶ ἀπέδρα ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτῆς.
hint: Abram: she is in your hands. Sarai mistreats her, and she runs away.

notes.text: The present imperative of χράομαι, the chain of GEN 12:16.
ἄν after ὡς, `ever`, as at 6:4; ἀρεστός, *acceptable, pleasing*, one sense of two glosses.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐναντίον σου.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: Εὗρεν δὲ αὐτὴν ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐπὶ τῆς πηγῆς τοῦ ὕδατος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, ἐπὶ τῆς πηγῆς ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ Σουρ.
hint: An angel of the Lord finds her by a spring in the desert, on the road to Shur.

notes.text: ἄγγελος is first *a messenger, envoy*; *a divine messenger, an angel* is its last.
ὕδωρ, plain text, as at 1:2.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds τοῦ θεοῦ; most witnesses do not.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου Αγαρ παιδίσκη Σαρας, πόθεν ἔρχῃ καὶ ποῦ πορεύῃ; καὶ εἶπεν Ἀπὸ προσώπου Σαρας τῆς κυρίας μου ἐγὼ ἀποδιδράσκω.
hint: Hagar, where have you come from, where are you going? I am running from my mistress.

notes.text: πορεύομαι, the chain of GEN 12:4, in the present.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου Ἀποστράφητι πρὸς τὴν κυρίαν σου καὶ ταπεινώθητι ὑπὸ τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῆς.
hint: Return to your mistress and submit to her.

notes.text: The aorist passive imperative of ταπεινόω, *to lower*, in the passive; the middle's *to humble oneself* last.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου Πληθύνων πληθυνῶ τὸ σπέρμα σου, καὶ οὐκ ἀριθμηθήσεται ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθους.
hint: I will greatly multiply your seed beyond counting.

notes.text: The words of GEN 3:16, there of pains, here of seed, with their chains.
πλῆθος is first *a great number, a throng, crowd, multitude*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου Ἰδοὺ σὺ ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχεις καὶ τέξῃ υἱὸν καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ισμαηλ, ὅτι ἐπήκουσεν κύριος τῇ ταπεινώσει σου.
hint: You will bear a son and call him Ishmael, for the Lord has heard your affliction.

notes.text: The Hebrew name holds the verb *šāmaʿ*, *to hear*, which the reason given repeats; the Greek gives the reason with ἐπακούω, and the name as a transliteration.
ἐπακούω is first *to listen*; ταπείνωσις, *humiliation, abasement*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: οὗτος ἔσται ἄγροικος ἄνθρωπος· αἱ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πάντας, καὶ αἱ χεῖρες πάντων ἐπʼ αὐτόν, καὶ κατὰ πρόσωπον πάντων τῶν ἀδελφῶν αὐτοῦ κατοικήσει.
hint: He will be a man of the country, his hand against all, dwelling before his brothers.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *pereʾ ʾādām*, *a wild ass of a man*. The Greek has *a man of the country*, ἄγροικος.
κατά, `down`, with πρόσωπον, the chain of GEN 3:8, without the article.

greek: καὶ ἐκάλεσεν Αγαρ τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου τοῦ λαλοῦντος πρὸς αὐτήν Σὺ ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἐπιδών με· ὅτι εἶπεν Καὶ γὰρ ἐνώπιον εἶδον ὀφθέντα μοι.
hint: Hagar names the Lord who spoke to her: You are the God who looked upon me.

notes.lemma: Σὺ ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἐπιδών με· ὅτι εἶπεν Καὶ γὰρ ἐνώπιον εἶδον ὀφθέντα μοι
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾattâ ʾēl rŏʾî kî ʾāmĕrâ hăgam hălōm rāʾîtî ʾaḥărê rōʾî*, *You are a God of seeing, for she said, Have I even here seen after him who sees me?* The Greek has *You are the God who looked upon me; for she said, For I saw face to face him who appeared to me*.
The participle of ἐπεῖδον, filed under ἐφοράω, the chain of GEN 4:4.
Filed inside ἐνώπιος, whose one translation is *face to face*: plain text, as at 11:28.
καὶ γάρ, `also for`, as at 9:5.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

greek: ἕνεκεν τούτου ἐκάλεσεν τὸ φρέαρ Φρέαρ οὗ ἐνώπιον εἶδον· ἰδοὺ ἀνὰ μέσον Καδης καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον Βαραδ.
hint: So the well is called the Well where I saw face to face, between Kadesh and Bered.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *Bĕʾēr laḥay rōʾî*, *Well of the Living One who sees me*. The Greek names it with Hagar's words of 16:13, *Well where I saw face to face*.
Capitalised as the first word of the well's name, and glossed as a name; the φρέαρ before it is the common noun, *a well*.
The adverb, *where*, plain; the name repeats ἐνώπιον εἶδον from 16:13.

reading: [[on account of|on account of, for the sake of, because of, for, as far as regards|ἕνεκα]] [[of this|of this, of the nearer, of what follows|οὗτος]] [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[the well|the well, the tank and cistern and reservoir, the oil jar|φρέαρ]] [[name:Φρέαρ]] where face to face [[I saw|I saw, I perceived, I beheld, I looked at|ὁράω]]; [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] of [[name:Καδης]] and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] of [[name:Βαραδ]].

names.gloss: (Φρέαρ, "a well", the first word of the name the verse gives the well, for Hebrew Bĕʾēr laḥay rōʾî)

greek: Καὶ ἔτεκεν Αγαρ τῷ Αβραμ υἱόν, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν Αβραμ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὃν ἔτεκεν αὐτῷ Αγαρ, Ισμαηλ.
hint: Hagar bears Abram a son, and Abram names him Ishmael.

notes.text: τίκτω, `brought into the world`, the chain of GEN 4:1.

reading: And [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] [[name:Αγαρ]] to the [[name:Αβραμ]] a son, and [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[name:Αβραμ]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of the son of him, whom [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] to him [[name:Αγαρ]], [[name:Ισμαηλ]].

greek: Αβραμ δὲ ἦν ὀγδοήκοντα ἓξ ἐτῶν, ἡνίκα ἔτεκεν Αγαρ τὸν Ισμαηλ τῷ Αβραμ.
hint: Abram is eighty-six when Hagar bears Ishmael.

notes.text: εἰμί of age, the state formula of GEN 1:2 in full, as at 12:4.

reading: [[name:Αβραμ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, of eighty of six of years, [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever|ἡνίκα]] [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] [[name:Αγαρ]] the [[name:Ισμαηλ]] to the [[name:Αβραμ]].
